authored_items.argument: Fixes the explicit A1 root, weight lattice, q,t field, affine reflections, length-zero symmetry, and finite Bernstein quotient polynomials.
Proves both positive- and negative-exponent cross-relation quotients by finite geometric sums.
Distinguishes q-affine maps and proves their finite-support operator independence by a Vandermonde determinant.
Defines the rank-one DAHA quotient with explicit affine-Hecke generators, length-zero symmetry, weight-lattice action, and independent q,t parameters.
Proves finite-support spanning by moving lattice letters left, length-zero symmetry right, and reducing repeated Hecke generators.
Checks the q-shift/reflection actions, Hecke quadratics, cross-relations, Laurent preservation, and quotient descent.
Records the polynomial module and generator actions; its well-definedness is established by the immediately preceding local relation check.
Uses the top affine substitution of each normal word and generic q-affine map independence to prove faithfulness for non-root-of-unity q and nonzero t.
Defines the rank-one symmetric q-difference operator; the local translation computation proves its DAHA origin.
Preserves the original skein and physical-knot interface scope while naming the missing maps, parameters, representation spaces, and model-specific operator data.
Removes apparent poles on symmetric Laurent polynomials, proves Weyl invariance, and computes the triangular diagonal eigenvalues.
Computes Y and Y^-1 on invariant functions and identifies every symmetric translation polynomial with a polynomial in D.
Proves the precise eigenvalue separation condition, constructs the normalized eigenbasis recursively, and identifies it as the symmetric DAHA Macdonald eigenbasis in type A1.
Computes P0 and P1 and their eigenvalues directly from the operator.
At q=1 the operator is scalar, so the first two orbit sums share an eigenvalue.
